name: Incline Smith Machine Press
movementPattern: Incline chest press - guided vertical/angled plane
grip: Overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width with wrists straight and stacked over forearms.
description: Press a fixed-track Smith machine barbell from the upper chest along guided vertical guide rods while seated on an incline bench, emphasizing the clavicular head of the pectoralis major with maximum stability.
setup: Position an adjustable incline bench at approximately 30 to 45 degrees inside the Smith machine.
Align the bench so the bar lowers across the upper clavicular chest (just below the collarbones) in a straight path.
Set safety catch pins just below the target bottom chest level.
Lie back with upper back and hips flat against the bench, feet firmly planted on the floor.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack the bar with a wrist rotation.
instructions: Lower the bar slowly under control toward your upper chest, allowing elbows to tuck naturally to about 45 to 60 degrees relative to your torso.
Touch the bar lightly to the upper chest or stop just above without bouncing off the ribcage.
Press the bar upward along the fixed track by contracting the upper pectorals and triceps until arms are extended with elbows softly unlocked.
Rotate wrists to engage the safety catches when the set is finished.
cues: Keep wrists straight and forearms vertical.
Control the descent to the clavicles.
commonMistakes: Setting the bench too far forward or backward, forcing unnatural shoulder internal rotation along the fixed track.
Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Flaring elbows out to 90 degrees, causing anterior shoulder impingement.

logging.example: Two 20 kg plates loaded (40 kg plates) plus 10 kg counterbalance bar: record 50 kg total effective load (or record 40 kg plate load + note bar weight).
logging.note: Smith machine bars vary in counterbalance weight (typically 5 kg to 15 kg); record total loaded plate mass and note machine bar tare.

variantNote: Incline barbell pressing performed on a fixed-track Smith machine. Eliminates stabilization requirements to isolate clavicular pectoral recruitment along a linear guided path.
